hero.h1: Tankless Water Heaters in Ravenswood, Chicago
hero.sub: In a tight basement or condo closet, a wall-mounted tankless heater frees up space and doesn't run out mid-shower. We install, repair and descale them, and tell you honestly if one fits. Our office is on Ravenswood Avenue.

img.alt: Plumber working on the copper water lines of a wall-mounted tankless water heater in a basement

blocks.body: A tankless heater fires only when a hot tap opens. Water passes through a heat exchanger and comes out hot for as long as you need it. Each unit has a flow limit, so it's sized for the most hot water your home uses at once.

blocks.body: Replacing two old tanks in a shared basement with two wall-mounted tankless heaters frees up floor space for storage or laundry. Each unit keeps its own hot water. The catch is gas and venting. Two tankless units can draw a lot of gas at once, so we check the meter and piping. Each one also needs its own vent, usually through an outside wall, which takes planning on a tight city lot.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of a Tankless Install
blocks.body: Gas line size and venting are the two big variables, especially in older buildings. Two units for a two-flat double the planning. We check first and quote one flat price.

items.q: Can a tankless heater use my chimney?
items.answer: No. It needs its own vent, usually through a side wall.

items.q: Can each unit in a two-flat have its own tankless heater?
items.answer: Yes, if the gas supply and venting allow it.

items.q: How often does it need descaling?
items.answer: About once a year for most homes.
Yes. We descale, clean sensors and replace failed parts.

items.q: Does a tankless heater need a new gas line?
items.answer: Sometimes. Older lines may be too small. We check before quoting.

items.q: Can a tankless heater fit in a condo closet?
items.answer: Often, if venting can reach an outside wall.
